summary: Sector sweep within one beat (27 E7a, 05 §8.4a M-32, P-12). A new last rule `region.sweep` (RULE.regionSweep, sweepPhases(n)) takes a beat with CROWD_MIN (4) or more creations (piece.appear / threat.emerge appears) as one maneuver. The sequencer places it first and holds back any later play on a swept subject until it ends; limelight and turns skip it; BaseMoment.swept feeds volleysOf's B-15 guard. The theme's sectorSweep tells a Nav cyan ring on the star, then a `sweep` finale ring sweeps out while each piece makes a quiet entrance in distance order (sweepOrder, ties by pk). The interpreter keeps swept pieces hidden until their entrances and puts one note on the star (sweepNote: '11 User Stories · 5 Bugs created in Sprint 13'). I reviewed the interrupted attempt and kept it (pace, maneuvers, director, contracts, events, theme files). I finished the interpreter and labels note, the finales sweep command, the gallery cell, the ledger rows, tests, docs and the drive step.

openQuestions.05 'what plays' table format: M-32 is a row in 05 §8.4a's existing three-column table (Rule | What | Notes), after M-31, so it sits inside the §8.4–§8.5 span that rulebook.test reads. P-12 is revised in place to name the sweep for 4+ creations.
openQuestions.GEOMETRY.starR: It exists (150, @shared/engine/solar/version) and is used directly for the tell ring (2.4×starR → 1.1×starR). No new constant was needed.

limitations: Upstream discrepancy, for the orchestrator: paceFacts counts pod-sprint's 20141 as Harbor's from its creation (created in Lantern, moved to Harbor on 10-02), but the knownThen board shows it elsewhere until the move. The sweep's cast and phases include it (17 subjects), and the chart reveals 16. sweep.test tolerates that one piece on Harbor and checks it is on the board by the round's end.
Halcyon (Comet, Nova, Quasar, Pulsar) has no creation burst, so the sweep saves nothing there. Check 2 runs on Halcyon only to show it's unchanged.
History marks only the carrier event's row as now; the other swept events don't get a row of their own while the sweep plays.
With no c.board (a crop without one), the sweep orders by distance from (0, 0) and scales the stops by the farthest piece.
